canonical_claim: There is no total computable decision procedure which, given an effective code for an arbitrary finite Post correspondence instance over a fixed finite alphabet, returns true exactly when some nonempty finite sequence of tile indices makes the concatenated upper words equal the concatenated lower words.
domain_and_universes: A fixed finite alphabet with at least two symbols; finite lists of pairs of finite words; nonempty finite lists of valid tile indices; and a concrete effective code type. Exact Lean types and the treatment of malformed codes remain open.
quantifiers: for every effectively encoded finite PCP instance
the instance has a solution iff there exists a nonempty finite valid index sequence whose upper and lower concatenations agree
there does not exist a total computable Boolean predicate deciding that solution predicate on every code
hypotheses: the alphabet and all tile words are finite and effectively encodable
the alphabet convention is nondegenerate and fixed independently of the input
the same ordered index sequence selects upper and lower words
conclusion: The uniform PCP solvability predicate is not computable/decidable in the selected effective encoding.

alternate_encodings.target: modified PCP, where the first tile is prescribed
alternate_encodings.relationship: nearby undecidable problem requiring a checked many-one reduction
candidate fixed-alphabet specialization/equivalence requiring checked coding transports
equivalent only after the chosen machine model is linked to mathlib's computability predicate

excluded_degenerate_cases: A decision procedure for one fixed instance, bounded-length matching, an empty index sequence, equality using different upper/lower index sequences, semi-decidability alone, and modified PCP alone do not establish the root. Unary or empty alphabet conventions may collapse the problem and cannot silently replace the fixed nondegenerate alphabet.

source_revisions.human_source_candidate: Emil L. Post, A variant of a recursively unsolvable problem, Bulletin of the AMS 52 (1946), 264-268, DOI 10.1090/S0002-9904-1946-08555-9

foundation_profile: Lean 4 dependent type theory; the exact classical, choice, quotient, and extensionality footprint remains open until a target and proof body are selected
tcb_profile: Lean kernel 4.29.0 and pinned mathlib are intended; exact imports and transitive declaration closure remain open
computation_profile: The root quantifies over effective decision procedures. No evaluator, oracle, external solver, reflection result, or generated certificate is credited at intake.
formal_system: Lean 4 + pinned mathlib under the rev-5.6 adapter
freshness_and_revocation_policy: Invalidate on source edition or interpretation, alphabet or encoding convention, match definition, malformed-code policy, canonical Lean target, toolchain/mathlib pin, foundation/TCB policy, validator, or assurance-standard change.
status_boundary: Self-tested planned intake only. It identifies the uniform PCP undecidability claim and rejects nearby substitutions, but does not freeze an effective encoding or exact Lean expression, establish H0, credit a formal proof, complete an audit, or complete the theorem.
